name: Uptime and redundancy
answer: These measures show how reliably a data center keeps its servers running and connected: network quality, backup power and contractual uptime. An AI training run can last weeks across thousands of chips, so an interruption costs more than in most workloads.

metrics.line: Continuous measurement of round-trip latency, loss rate, and utilization on the facility's internal fabric and external transit.
metrics.label: Network latency, packet loss, and bandwidth

metrics.line: Battery state of health and remaining runtime under current load, and on-site fuel measured in hours of generator operation at load.
metrics.label: UPS battery health and generator runtime

metrics.line: Delivered availability measured against the contracted service level, conventionally quoted in nines.
metrics.label: SLA uptime compliance

reading.body:
Uptime in a data center is measured three ways: network quality, backup power, and contracted availability.

The three metrics cover different failure paths. Network latency, packet loss, and bandwidth are measured continuously on the internal fabric and external transit, so they catch degradation before it becomes an outage. Battery health and generator runtime are measured as remaining capacity under current load, which is the only version of that number that matters during an actual event. SLA compliance is the contractual scorecard, quoted in nines, and it is the one figure a customer can hold the operator to.

The stakes are higher for AI than for most workloads because a training run can last weeks across thousands of chips. A brief interruption does not just delay a job, it can waste the work already done. That makes backup power and network stability operational inputs to AI capability rather than facilities housekeeping.

What this data does not cover is the cost of redundancy, the fuel supply chain behind generator hours, or how any of these measures are verified. It names what is tracked, not what the thresholds are or who audits them.
